requirements.requirement: The system must validate that the confidence score calculation returns a normalized value between 0 and 1 for valid complete input data.
The system must verify that completeness, recency, and agreement components are each included in the confidence calculation output.
The system must confirm that increasing missing data reduces the completeness component score in unit tests.
The system must confirm that older data timestamps reduce the recency component score in unit tests.
The system must confirm that higher variance across measures reduces the agreement component score in unit tests.
The system must validate that the final confidence score changes when any individual component (completeness, recency, agreement) is altered.
The system must handle missing input data without crashing and return a valid confidence score with reduced completeness.
The system must handle stale data inputs and reflect reduced recency in the computed confidence score.
The system must handle conflicting measures and reflect reduced agreement in the computed confidence score.
The system must include the confidence object in evaluation API responses for providers when requested.
The system must include the confidence object in evaluation API responses for clinical trials when requested.
The system must ensure the confidence object in API responses conforms to the schema defined in EVAL-CONF-ST-001.
The system must ensure that API responses without confidence logic (feature disabled or unavailable) do not break existing response contracts.
The system must return deterministic confidence scores for identical input datasets across repeated test runs.
The system must ensure integration tests validate that confidence scores are serialized and returned in JSON responses without null fields when data is present.
